description: Real open-source applications with genuine, exploitable weaknesses. Fetched at a pinned revision rather than vendored: these trees are collectively larger than the whole of this repository, and they are code we did not write and must not edit.
ground_truth_status: pygoat labelled — 46 cases in answers/ (34 vulnerable, 12 traps) at the pinned revision; webgoat, dvja, nodegoat and juice-shop not yet. See docs/EXTERNAL-CORPORA.md

sources.name: webgoat
sources.license_note: GitHub reports NOASSERTION; read LICENSE.txt in the checkout and record the result here before any use that redistributes or publishes from it
sources.notes: Spring MVC, JDBC and JPA idioms. The reason to include it: Spring data binding and ORM-level injection are where Java tools separate.

sources.name: dvja
sources.notes: Smaller Java target than WebGoat; useful as a second Java opinion.

sources.name: pygoat
sources.notes: Django. Labelled at this revision: 46 cases, read from the code and checked against the app's own Solutions/solution.md, then against RealVuln (github.com/kolega-ai/Real-Vuln-Benchmark), whose 88 PyGoat entries carry the same line numbers as this checkout.

sources.name: juice-shop
sources.notes: TypeScript and Angular; the only realistic TypeScript target in this set.
